focus: Angle 5 invocation mechanics: per-runtime command mirrors, seven brief adapters versus a six-row doc table, and the two universal fallbacks (name-and-ask, load-and-follow)
noveltyJustification: All 8 findings are new: this is the first iteration to enumerate runtime command mirrors, compare the hooks tree with the hook reference, and test the model-invocation assumption against repository rules.
keyQuestions: Can a model start a slash command by itself on Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi, Cursor, Devin and DSH, and what fallback exists where it cannot?
answeredQuestions: Can a model start a slash command by itself on Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi, Cursor, Devin and DSH, and what fallback exists where it cannot?
ruledOut: Giving the model the slash string so it invokes the command: no runtime exposes slash commands as model tools and no rule instructs typing one
Treating runtime parity as a per-runtime brief problem: one renderer feeds every transport, so divergence lives in command mirroring and a stale documentation row

label: Every runtime except Devin mirrors the command tree into a slash surface, in different shapes: 45 markdown files in .claude/commands group dirs, symlinked groups in .opencode/commands, 46 flat files in .cursor/commands, 45 in .codex/prompts, 46 in .pi/prompts and 45 in .dsh/prompts, while .devin has no commands or prompts directory at all.
Devin is the only runtime where a command cannot be typed even by the user, so a Devin session reaches a command workflow only through the advisor brief or a model following the command doc.

Advisor brief adapters exist for seven runtimes in the hooks tree, but the hook reference per-runtime table lists six and omits DSH although .skilled/hooks/skill-advisor/dsh/prompt-advisor.mjs and its README document an agent/pre-step adapter registered through .dsh/plugins/repo-guards: documentation drift, not a missing capability.

Delivery channels are not interchangeable: additionalContext JSON on Claude, Codex, Cursor and Devin; output.system for the OpenCode plugin; a model-visible message on Pi; an operator-step notice on DSH, all fed by the single renderAdvisorBrief renderer, so brief wording has one change point.

No model-facing rule instructs the model to type a slash command: AGENTS.md Gate 2 asks for the hook brief and a node advisor call and a SKILL ROUTING line, and the deep-research skill states it is invoked exclusively through its user-typed command.

The repository already expects the model to execute an entry point it was told about: the advisor outage fallback prints a literal node skill-advisor.cjs advisor_recommend line for the model to run, a precedent that covers shell entry points but not slash commands.

The only AGENTS.md text naming a command bridge resolves a tie in the bridge favour, stating that command-spec-kit wins alongside cli-* for iteration phrases, so the model-facing rules know bridge ids and slash keys but never a command-to-workflow instruction.

Because a command file is repository markdown and every workflow it routes to is also a repository file, a model can execute a command workflow without runtime slash expansion; that load-and-follow path exists on all seven runtimes including Devin and is the only universal fallback.
Hook reference documents six runtimes while seven adapters exist; DSH row is missing
